sources.citation: Stadler M, et al. Theoretical effect of hyperventilation on speed of recovery and risk of rehypnotization following recovery: a Gas Man simulation. BMC Anesthesiology. 2012;12:22.
sources.note: Table 1 reports the Gas Man isoflurane blood:gas and tissue:gas coefficients used here, in the same table already cited for sevoflurane.

sources.citation: Yasuda N, Targ AG, Eger EI II. Solubility of I-653, sevoflurane, isoflurane, and halothane in human tissues. Anesthesia & Analgesia. 1989;69(3):370-373.
sources.note: Primary human-tissue study reporting an isoflurane brain:blood partition coefficient of 1.57 +/- 0.10 at 37 degrees C. Same paper already cited for sevoflurane's and desflurane's tissue-solubility models.

sources.citation: Malviya S, Lerman J. The blood/gas solubilities of sevoflurane, isoflurane, halothane, and serum constituent concentrations in neonates and adults. Anesthesiology. 1990;72(5):793-796.
sources.note: Confirms isoflurane's blood:gas partition coefficient was measured directly in adult humans and found to differ from neonates. The specific adult value was not independently re-derived from the abstract alone; version 0.2.0 uses the Gas Man value of 1.3 from Stadler et al. above.

sources.citation: Kelly JM, Kong K-L. Accuracy of ten isoflurane vaporisers in current clinical use. Anaesthesia. 2011;66(8):682-688.
sources.note: Studies the two standard isoflurane vaporizers in current clinical use (Penlon Sigma Delta, Datex-Ohmeda Isotec 5), both calibrated 0-5%. Used here as max_delivered_concentration_percent. This is a device-capability limit on the delivered-concentration control, not a scientific model parameter; it does not affect the governing equations.

sources.citation: Nickalls RWD, Mapleson WW. Age-related iso-MAC charts for isoflurane, sevoflurane and desflurane in man. British Journal of Anaesthesia. 2003;91(2):170-174.
sources.note: MAC is age-dependent; this project's reference-adult model has no age parameter, so mac_percent uses the flat adult value from Stadler et al. above (same paper already cited for partition coefficients: 'MAC values that we used in our Gas Man simulations are: desflurane 6%, sevoflurane 2%, isoflurane 1.2%'), not an age-adjusted one. Used as the controller's starting delivered-concentration default (1 MAC), not a governing-equation parameter.
